newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai support fund to extend loans from Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: New Thai support fund to extend loans from Sept 30.

text.p: Thailand's new 10 billion baht stock market support fund will start extending loans to cash strapped investors from September 30 after signing loan contracts with borrowers, brokers said on Monday.

Brokers said the state-run Government Savings Bank, which operates the fund, told brokerages it would start signing loan contracts arranged through brokerage firms from September 26. Loan disbursement would be available from end-September.
They said the bank set a condition that it would only accept as collateral shares that borrowing investors had bought before September 10.

The bank said the government fund would charge a concessional 11 percent lending rate on loans of up to two years sought by investors facing the prospect of being forced to sell shares to pay off debts.

The Thai finance ministry last week initiated the new support fund in a bid to halt an extended share slide. The Bangkok bourse has fallen to a near three-year low on weak economic fundamentals and jitters before expected politicial changes.
The fund, together with buying by a separate 15.7 billion baht private sector fund, has fuelled a strong rally on the bourse in the past few sessions.
The SET index gained 20.15 points, or 1.94 percent, to 1,059.80 during the Monday morning session.
